scene_report.narration_text: In March 2024, Kendrick Lamar ignited a massive controversy by rejecting the idea that he, Drake, and J. Cole were rap's Big Three.
Kendrick declared there was only one king, prompting Drake to fire back with the diss track Push Ups.
Kendrick responded by unleashing Euphoria, a brutal six-minute attack on his rival.
The conflict turned deeply personal when Drake released Family Matters, making explosive allegations about Kendrick's private life.
scene_report.main_action: lying on a dark wooden desk

scene_report.narration_text: Less than an hour later, Kendrick shocked listeners with Meet the Grahams, firing back with disturbing claims about Drake's family.
On May 4, Kendrick dropped the devastating track Not Like Us, which accused Drake of serious misconduct.
While Drake denied these allegations, the song exploded across the internet, becoming a global anthem.
scene_report.main_action: displaying a viral social media feed

scene_report.narration_text: Millions danced to the track, which ultimately won five Grammy Awards.
What began as a battle for the rap throne became one of hip-hop's most unforgettable rivalries.
